territorial_scope.description: Applies to liability arising from acts occurring directly in California.

evidence.quote: This section shall apply to the adjudication of liability and the imposition of any damages or other remedies in cases in which the liability, damages, and other remedies arise from acts occurring directly in this state.

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends California Civil Code § 3344.1 to impose liability on persons who produce, distribute or make available a deceased personality's digital replica in expressive audiovisual works or sound recordings without consent, with listed exemptions. Effective date not stated in the provided text.
summary.long: Section 1 states legislative intent to protect intellectual property from exploitation. Section 2 amends Civil Code § 3344.1 on use of a deceased personality's name, voice, signature, photograph or likeness. Subdivision (a)(1) makes unconsented use on products, merchandise, goods, advertising or solicitation liable for the greater of $750 or actual damages, plus profits not counted in actual damages; punitive damages and attorney's fees are available. Subdivision (a)(2) makes a person who produces, distributes or makes available a digital replica of a deceased personality's voice or likeness in an expressive audiovisual work or sound recording without consent liable for the greater of $10,000 or actual damages, unless an exception applies: news, public affairs or sports broadcasts; comment, criticism, scholarship, satire or parody; certain documentary or biographical representations; fleeting or incidental use; or advertisements for such works. A digital replica is defined as a computer-generated, highly realistic, readily identifiable representation. Other subdivisions cover transferability and succession of rights, a 70-year post-death limit, claims registration with the Secretary of State, cumulative remedies, application to acts occurring directly in California, and retroactivity for personalities who died before January 1, 1985. The document reproduces the amended section in full and does not mark which text is new.

entities.name: Secretary of State (California)
entities.function: Receives and posts registrations of successor-in-interest and licensee claims to deceased personality rights, prescribes the claim form, and may microfilm or destroy filings and post the registry online.

notes: Only SEC. 2 amends a law (Civil Code § 3344.1). SEC. 1 is a statement of legislative intent referring to all intellectual property, while the amended section concerns the right of publicity. The text carries no markings separating new from restated text, so the new digital-replica provisions in § 3344.1(a)(2) and (B) cannot be distinguished from unchanged text; coding is based on the text as presented and should be checked against the enrolled bill. No effective-date section appears in the text provided. Government Code § 12195 and Probate Code § 240 are cited but not reproduced.

thresholds.value_text: died within 70 years prior to January 1, 1985
thresholds.measurement: period measured back from January 1, 1985 to the date of death
thresholds.consequence: A natural person who died within 70 years before January 1, 1985 is included in the definition of deceased personality.
thresholds.conditions: Applies in addition to the commercial-value test in the first sentence of the definition.

evidence.quote: A “deceased personality” shall include, without limitation, any such natural person who has died within 70 years prior to January 1, 1985.

thresholds.variable_text: years after death within which an action may be brought
thresholds.value_text: not brought after the expiration of 70 years after the death of the deceased personality
thresholds.measurement: time from the death of the deceased personality to the use complained of
thresholds.consequence: No action may be brought under this section for a use occurring more than 70 years after the death of the deceased personality.
thresholds.conditions: Applies to use of the name, voice, signature, photograph, or likeness of a deceased personality under this section.

evidence.quote: An action shall not be brought under this section by reason of any use of a deceased personality’s name, voice, signature, photograph, or likeness occurring after the expiration of 70 years after the death of the deceased personality.

thresholds.value_text: any deceased personality who died prior to January 1, 1985

thresholds.variable_text: year of action taken to exercise rights (relative to May 1, 2007)
thresholds.value_text: if an action was taken prior to May 1, 2007
thresholds.measurement: date on which the action to exercise rights was taken
thresholds.consequence: The exercise of rights is not affected by subdivision (b), and the rights vest solely in the persons described in subdivision (d), other than a disinherited person.
thresholds.conditions: Applies to a deceased personality who died prior to January 1, 1985, where the exercise was not successfully challenged in court by a person described in subdivision (b).

evidence.quote: if an action was taken prior to May 1, 2007, to exercise rights recognized under this section

thresholds.variable_text: aggregate interest in the rights held by persons exercising them
thresholds.value_text: those persons who, in the aggregate, are entitled to more than a one-half interest in the rights
thresholds.measurement: aggregate ownership share of the persons entitled under subdivision (d)
thresholds.consequence: Those persons may exercise the rights on behalf of and for the benefit of all persons entitled after the death of a person.

evidence.quote: by those persons who, in the aggregate, are entitled to more than a one-half interest in the rights
“deceased personality” means any natural person whose name, voice, signature, photograph, or likeness has commercial value at the time of that person’s death, or because of that person’s death
“Digital replica” means a computer-generated, highly realistic electronic representation that is readily identifiable as the voice or visual likeness of an individual
“Audiovisual work” means a work that consists of a series of related images that are intrinsically intended to be shown by the use of machines or devices

“photograph” means any photograph or photographic reproduction, still or moving, or any videotape or live television transmission, of any person, such that the deceased personality is readily identifiable

obligations.summary: The Secretary of State must post filed successor-in-interest or licensee claims, together with the entire registry of such claims, on its internet website. The Secretary of State may also microfilm or reproduce filings, which is a permission and is not coded.

obligations.conditional_on: A document is filed under Civil Code 3344.1 (successor or licensee claims)

evidence.quote: the Secretary of State shall post the document along with the entire registry

obligations.summary: A person claiming to be a successor in interest to a deceased personality's rights, or a licensee, who chooses to register the claim must file a verified form with the Secretary of State containing the listed information and pay the fee. The text does not specify further addressee categories.
obligations.applies_from: On registering a claim with the Secretary of State
obligations.conditional_on: The claimant chooses to register a claim under Civil Code 3344.1(f)(2)

evidence.quote: The form shall be verified and shall include the name and date of death of the deceased personality

enforcement.triggered_by: Use of a deceased personality's name, voice, signature, photograph, or likeness, without prior consent, on or in products, merchandise, or goods, or for advertising, selling, or soliciting purchases of products, merchandise, goods, or services
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Greater of seven hundred fifty dollars ($750) or actual damages, plus profits attributable to the use not counted in actual damages; punitive damages may also be awarded; prevailing party may recover attorney's fees and costs
enforcement.penalty_formula: Greater of $750 or actual damages suffered by the injured party or parties, plus non-duplicative profits attributable to the use

evidence.quote: the person who violated the section shall be liable to the injured party or parties in an amount equal to the greater of seven hundred fifty dollars ($750) or the actual damages suffered by the injured party or parties

enforcement.authority: None named; private action under Civil Code § 3344.1

enforcement.max_penalty_text: Greater of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) or actual damages suffered by a person controlling the rights to the deceased personality's likeness
enforcement.penalty_formula: Greater of $10,000 or actual damages suffered by a person controlling the rights to the deceased personality's likeness

evidence.quote: shall be liable to any injured party in an amount equal to the greater of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) or the actual damages suffered by a person controlling the rights

events.note: The text gives no enactment, signature, publication, entry-into-force, application, phase-in, deadline, sunset, expiry or repeal date for this act. Dates in the amended section (January 1, 1985; May 1, 2007; 70 years after death) refer to earlier law, past actions or rights periods and are not events of this instrument.
